statement: For the half-filled [Hubbard model](c:hubbard-model) on a [connected](c:connected-graph) [bipartite](c:bipartite-graph) lattice $\Lambda = A \sqcup B$ with uniform repulsion $U > 0$, the [ground state](c:ground-state) is unique up to spin degeneracy and has total spin $S = \tfrac12\,\big||A| - |B|\big|$.

hypotheses.text: $|\Lambda|$ is even and the number of electrons is $N = |\Lambda|$ in the [Hubbard model](c:hubbard-model).
The hopping $t_{xy} = t_{yx}$ is real and vanishes when $x$ and $y$ lie in the same set of the [bipartite](c:bipartite-graph) partition.
The bonds with $t_{xy} \ne 0$ form a [connected graph](c:connected-graph) on $\Lambda$.
The on-site repulsion is $U_x = U > 0$ at every site.

conclusion: The ground states form one spin multiplet, and its total spin is $S = \tfrac12\,\big||A| - |B|\big|$.

proofs.name: Partial particle-hole map, spin-reflection positivity and continuity in U
proofs.slogan: Map the half-filled repulsive model to an attractive one, prove uniqueness by positivity of the wave-function matrix, and read off the spin at large U.
proofs.scope: Outline of Lieb's proof for uniform U > 0 at half filling.

roles.why: Half filling makes the $S^z = 0$ sector map to the sector $N_\uparrow = N_\downarrow$ of the attractive model, where the wave function is a square matrix.
Only hops between the two sets keep their sign under the partial particle-hole transformation.
Connectivity of the lattice makes the configuration graph connected, which forces a positive semidefinite ground state to be definite.
A uniform $U$ makes the term $U N_\uparrow$ a constant after the transformation, so the two spins see the same one-body operator.

steps.slogan: Reduce to the sector with total $S^z = 0$, which meets every spin multiplet once.
steps.detail: The [Hamiltonian](c:hamiltonian) commutes with total spin, and at even $N$ every multiplet has one vector with $S^z_{tot} = 0$. So a unique ground vector in this sector gives one ground multiplet.

steps.slogan: Transform the down-spin electrons into holes to obtain an attractive Hubbard model.
steps.detail: The map $c_{x\downarrow} \mapsto \varepsilon(x) d^\dagger_{x\downarrow}$ of the [creation and annihilation operators](c:creation-and-annihilation-operators), with $\varepsilon = \pm 1$ on $A$ and $B$, keeps the hopping between $A$ and $B$. It turns $U n_\uparrow n_\downarrow$ into $U n_\uparrow - U n_\uparrow n_\downarrow$, and the sector becomes $N_\uparrow = N_\downarrow = |\Lambda|/2$ of the attractive model.

steps.slogan: Show that replacing the wave-function matrix $W$ by $|W|$ does not raise the energy.
steps.detail: Write the state as a matrix $W(X, Y)$ in up and down configurations. For Hermitian $W$ the energy depends on the eigenvalues $w_\alpha$ through $w_\alpha^2$ and through $-U w_\alpha w_\beta$ terms, so $|W|$, a [positive semidefinite matrix](c:positive-semidefinite-matrix), is also a ground state.

steps.slogan: Prove that the ground state is unique with an invariant-subspace argument.
steps.detail: For a ground state $W \ge 0$ the range and the kernel are invariant under the hopping and the density operators. Connectivity of the configuration graph forces the kernel to be zero, and two independent ground states would give a singular $|W|$.

steps.slogan: Show that the ground state spin is constant in $U$ because the ground level never crosses.
steps.detail: The lowest eigenvalue in the sector is simple for every $U > 0$, so its eigenprojection is continuous in $U$. The eigenvalue $S(S+1)$ of the [Casimir operator](c:casimir-operator) is then continuous with discrete values, hence constant.

steps.slogan: Identify the spin at large repulsion with the Heisenberg model and apply Lieb-Mattis.
steps.detail: For large $U$ second-order perturbation theory gives the [Heisenberg model](c:heisenberg-model) with $J_{xy} = 2t_{xy}^2/U$ on the bonds of $\Lambda$. Lieb-Mattis gives it a unique ground multiplet of spin $\tfrac12||A| - |B||$, and continuity carries this spin to every $U > 0$.

concepts.c:connected-graph: Connectivity of the hopping graph is needed for the uniqueness argument.

concepts.c:hamiltonian: The Hubbard Hamiltonian commutes with total spin, which reduces the problem to one sector.
concepts.c:creation-and-annihilation-operators: The partial particle-hole map acts on the down-spin creation and annihilation operators.
concepts.c:positive-semidefinite-matrix: Spin-reflection positivity produces a positive semidefinite ground state matrix.

new_concepts.name: ground state
new_concepts.reminder: A ground state is an eigenvector of a Hamiltonian for the lowest point of its spectrum.
new_concepts.definition: Let $H$ be a [self-adjoint operator](c:self-adjoint-operator) on a Hilbert space that is bounded below, the [Hamiltonian](c:hamiltonian) of a quantum system. Its ground state energy is $E_0=\inf\sigma(H)=\inf_{\|\psi\|=1}\langle\psi,H\psi\rangle$. A ground state is a unit vector $\psi$ with $H\psi=E_0\psi$, and it exists exactly when $E_0$ is an [eigenvalue](c:eigenvalue) of $H$.

new_concepts.name: Hubbard model
new_concepts.reminder: The Hubbard model describes electrons that hop between lattice sites with amplitude $t$ and repel with energy $U$ on one site.
new_concepts.definition: On a finite [graph](c:graph) $\Lambda=(V,E)$, the Hubbard model is the [Hamiltonian](c:hamiltonian) $H=-t\sum_{\{x,y\}\in E}\sum_{s=\uparrow,\downarrow}(c^\dagger_{xs}c_{ys}+c^\dagger_{ys}c_{xs})+U\sum_{x\in V}n_{x\uparrow}n_{x\downarrow}$ on the fermionic [Fock space](c:fock-space). Here $c^\dagger_{xs}$ and $c_{xs}$ are the fermionic [creation and annihilation operators](c:creation-and-annihilation-operators) of an electron with spin $s$ at $x$, and $n_{xs}=c^\dagger_{xs}c_{xs}$. The hopping amplitude is $t>0$, and the on-site repulsion is $U\ge0$.

statement: For a [Heisenberg model](c:heisenberg-model) on a connected [bipartite](c:bipartite-graph) bond graph, with antiferromagnetic bonds between the sublattices and ferromagnetic bonds inside them, the [ground state](c:ground-state) is a single multiplet of total spin $\bar S = |S_A - S_B|$, and the lowest energies $E(S)$ increase strictly for $S \ge \bar S$.

hypotheses.text: $\Lambda = A \sqcup B$ with $A, B$ nonempty, each site carries a spin $s_x \ge 1/2$, and $H = \sum J_{xy} S_x\cdot S_y$ is a [Heisenberg model](c:heisenberg-model).
$J_{xy} \ge 0$ when $x, y$ lie in different sets and $J_{xy} \le 0$ when they lie in the same set.
The graph of bonds with $J_{xy} \ne 0$ is a [connected graph](c:connected-graph).

conclusion: The ground states form one multiplet of total spin $\bar S = |S_A - S_B|$ with $S_A = \sum_{x \in A} s_x$ and $S_B = \sum_{x \in B} s_x$. Also $E(S) < E(S')$ for $\bar S \le S < S'$, and the ground state coefficients carry the Marshall signs.

proofs.name: Marshall signs, Perron-Frobenius and a solvable comparison model
proofs.slogan: Make the Hamiltonian a matrix with nonpositive off-diagonal entries, get positive ground vectors in each sector, and read off their spin from a solvable model.
proofs.scope: The whole theorem.

roles.why: The partition defines the Marshall signs and the comparison model $S_A \cdot S_B$, whose spectrum gives the value $\bar S$.
The sign conditions make every off-diagonal entry nonpositive after the Marshall sign change.
A connected bond graph makes the matrix irreducible in each sector, which gives uniqueness and strict positivity.

steps.slogan: Change the signs of the basis vectors so that all off-diagonal entries become nonpositive.
steps.detail: With $|\sigma\rangle' = (-1)^{\sum_{x \in A}(s_x - \sigma_x)}|\sigma\rangle$, a move of one unit of $S^z$ between $A$ and $B$ flips the sign and a move inside a set keeps it. The sign conditions on $J_{xy}$ then make every off-diagonal matrix element of $H$ nonpositive.

steps.slogan: Show that the matrix is irreducible in each sector of fixed total $S^z$.
steps.detail: Two configurations with the same total $S^z$ differ by a surplus at some site and a deficit at another. A shortest bond path between them carries one unit across, with the moves ordered so that every move is possible. Induction on the distance joins any two configurations.

steps.slogan: Apply Perron-Frobenius in each sector to get a unique positive ground vector.
steps.detail: The matrix $c - H_M$ is nonnegative and [irreducible](c:irreducible-matrix), so its top [eigenvector](c:eigenvector) is unique with positive coordinates. The [Casimir operator](c:casimir-operator) $S_{tot}\cdot S_{tot}$ commutes with $H$, so this ground vector has a definite total spin.

steps.slogan: Compare with the solvable model $S_A \cdot S_B$, whose ground vector is also nonnegative.
steps.detail: From $S_A\cdot S_B = \frac12(C - C_A - C_B)$ and the Clebsch-Gordan rule, its sector-$M$ ground vector is unique with spin $\max(|M|, \bar S)$ and has nonnegative coordinates. A positive vector and a nonnegative nonzero vector are not orthogonal, so both vectors have the same total spin.

steps.slogan: Translate the sector ground states into the ground multiplet and the ordering of $E(S)$.
steps.detail: Each sector minimum is $e(M) = \min_{S \ge |M|} E(S)$ with a unique minimizer of spin $\max(|M|, \bar S)$. The smallest sector gives the unique ground multiplet of spin $\bar S$, and the sector $M = S$ gives $E(S) < E(S')$ for $\bar S \le S < S'$ for this [Hamiltonian](c:hamiltonian).

concepts.c:heisenberg-model: The theorem is about the Heisenberg model with sublattice sign conditions.
concepts.c:bipartite-graph: The bipartite structure defines the Marshall signs and the value of the ground state spin.
concepts.c:ground-state: The theorem identifies the ground state multiplet and its total spin.
concepts.c:connected-graph: Connectivity of the bond graph gives irreducibility in each sector.
concepts.c:irreducible-matrix: Irreducibility is the hypothesis of Perron-Frobenius that gives a simple eigenvalue.
concepts.c:eigenvector: The ground vector in each sector is the Perron eigenvector with positive coordinates.
concepts.c:casimir-operator: The Casimir operator measures the total spin of the ground vectors.
concepts.c:hamiltonian: The ordering statement concerns the lowest eigenvalues of the Hamiltonian in each spin sector.

source.ref: B. Nachtergaele, W. Spitzer and S. Starr, Ferromagnetic ordering of energy levels, J. Stat. Phys. 116 (2004), arXiv:math-ph/0308006v2, Theorem 1.1 on p. 2 and its proof sketch on pp. 3-4.
source.note: The steps follow the Perron-Frobenius argument of the sketch. The comparison step uses the non-orthogonality of positive ground vectors, as in the original paper of Lieb and Mattis, instead of the continuity argument of the sketch.

statement: For the spin-1 AKLT chain $H_N = \sum_{n=1}^{N-1} P_2(S_n + S_{n+1})$, the [ground state](c:ground-state) space is four-dimensional and the [spectral gap](c:spectral-gap) is at least $1 - \sqrt3/2$ for every $N \ge 2$ and for every infinite-volume ground state that is a weak-* limit.

hypotheses.text: Each bond carries the [orthogonal projection](c:orthogonal-projection) $P_2(S_n + S_{n+1})$ onto total spin $2$ of the pair, on the [tensor product](c:tensor-product) $(\mathbb{C}^3)^{\otimes N}$ with open ends.
The infinite-volume ground state $\omega$ is a limit of finite-volume ground states in the [weak-* topology](c:weak-star-topology).

conclusion: $\dim\ker H_N = 4$ and $H_N \ge (1 - \tfrac{\sqrt3}{2})(1 - G_N)$ for all $N \ge 2$. Also $\omega(\delta(X)^*\delta^2(X)) \ge (1 - \tfrac{\sqrt3}{2})\,\omega(\delta(X)^*\delta(X))$ for every local $X$.

proofs.name: Martingale method with an improved overlap bound
proofs.slogan: Grow the chain block by block, control the overlap of neighbouring ground state projections, and compute that overlap exactly from product ground states.
proofs.scope: Outline of the proof of Spitzer and Starr (2003), Theorem 2.1, Corollary 2.3 and Section 4. The closed-form eigenvalues of the overlap matrix are taken from the source.

roles.why: The projection interaction makes the chain frustration-free and gives product ground states after the Kennedy-Tasaki transformation.
A weak-* limit lets the finite-volume gap inequality pass to the infinite chain.

steps.slogan: Bound energies and cross terms of ground state projections with two Cauchy-Schwarz estimates.
steps.detail: Lemma 2.2 gives $\langle\psi|H\psi\rangle \ge \gamma|\langle\psi|(1-G)\varphi\rangle|^2/\langle\varphi|(1-G)\varphi\rangle$ and $|\langle\psi|G\varphi\rangle|^2 \le \|\psi\|^2\|\varphi\|^2\langle G\rangle_\varphi(1-\langle G\rangle_\varphi)$ for $\psi \perp \varphi$.

steps.slogan: Grow the chain by $n$ sites and keep a weighted energy bound by induction.
steps.detail: If $\varepsilon_{m,n} < 1/2$, then for $\psi \perp G(1,N)$ one has $\langle\psi|H(1,N)\psi\rangle \ge \gamma_{m+n}(\alpha\|\psi_1\|^2 + \beta\|\psi_2\|^2)$ with $\alpha = (\sqrt{1-\varepsilon}-\sqrt{\varepsilon})^2 \le \beta$. The step splits $H(1,N) = H(1,N-n) + H(N-n,N)$ and ends with a positive quadratic form.

steps.slogan: Turn the weighted bound into a uniform gap and pass to weak-* limits.
steps.detail: Since $\alpha = 1 - 2\sqrt{\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)}$, $\inf_N \gamma(N) \ge \gamma_{m+n}\alpha$. For a local $X$, the vector $[H,X]\psi_N$ is orthogonal to the ground states, which gives the inequality for $\omega_N$ and then for its limit $\omega$.

steps.slogan: Turn the four [ground states](c:ground-state) into product states with the Kennedy-Tasaki unitary.
steps.detail: After $U = \prod_{j<k} e^{i\pi S^z_j S^x_k}$ the ground states are $\bigotimes \varphi_k$ with $\varphi_{1,2} = (|0\rangle \pm \sqrt2|{+}\rangle)/\sqrt3$ and $\varphi_{3,4} = (|0\rangle \pm \sqrt2|{-}\rangle)/\sqrt3$. Their Gram matrix has entries $(\pm 1/3)^N$ off the diagonal, and its inverse gives the ground state projection.

steps.slogan: Compute $\varepsilon(m,n)$ as the fifth eigenvalue of a $16 \times 16$ overlap matrix.
steps.detail: The matrix of $G(-m,0)G(0,n)G(-m,0)$ in a product basis has four eigenvalues $1$. The [Clebsch-Gordan](c:clebsch-gordan-coefficient) decomposition $V(5) \oplus 3V(3) \oplus 2V(1)$ and Schur's lemma give the others in closed form, for example $\lambda_5(m,n)$.

steps.slogan: Insert $\varepsilon_{1,1} = 1/4$ and $\gamma_2 = 1$ into the uniform gap bound.
steps.detail: The source finds $\varepsilon_{1,1} = \lambda_5(1,1) = 1/4$, and $\gamma_2 = 1$ because $P_2$ is a projection. Then $\inf_N\gamma(N) \ge 1 - 2\sqrt{3/16} = 1 - \sqrt3/2$, and the infinite-volume bound is the same.

concepts.c:ground-state: The ground states form the kernel of the frustration-free AKLT Hamiltonian.
concepts.c:spectral-gap: The spectral gap above the ground states is the quantity that the theorem bounds.
concepts.c:orthogonal-projection: Each bond term and each ground state projection is an orthogonal projection.
concepts.c:tensor-product: The chain lives on the tensor product of the spin-1 site spaces.
concepts.c:weak-star-topology: Infinite-volume ground states arise as weak-* limits of finite-volume ground states.
concepts.c:clebsch-gordan-coefficient: The Clebsch-Gordan decomposition splits the overlap matrix into SU(2) blocks.

statement: In the [Hubbard model](c:hubbard-model) with one hole, nonnegative hopping and $U = \infty$, if the hole connects all spin configurations of each sector, then every [ground state](c:ground-state) has total spin $S_{\max} = N_e/2$ and the ground state space has dimension $2S_{\max} + 1$.

hypotheses.text: The hopping matrix $T = (t_{x,y})$ is real and symmetric with $t_{x,y} \ge 0$, a [nonnegative matrix](c:nonnegative-matrix).
$N_e = N_s - 1$ and $U = \infty$, that is, the [self-adjoint operator](c:self-adjoint-operator) $\tilde H = P_0 H_{\mathrm{hop}}$ on the states with no doubly occupied site.
In each sector of fixed $S^{(3)}_{\mathrm{tot}}$, the basis states are joined by chains of nonzero matrix elements of $\tilde H$, so the matrix is an [irreducible matrix](c:irreducible-matrix).

conclusion: Every ground state of $\tilde H$ has $S_{\mathrm{tot}} = S_{\max} = N_e/2$, and the ground state space has dimension exactly $2S_{\max} + 1$.

proofs.name: Hole hopping, Cauchy-Schwarz comparison and Perron-Frobenius
proofs.slogan: The hole hops with real nonpositive matrix elements, so a ferromagnetic state is a ground state, and Perron-Frobenius makes it the only one in each sector.
proofs.scope: Outline of the proof in Tasaki (1998), Lemma 4.2, Theorem 4.1, Theorem 4.3 and Definition 4.4, pp. 25-29.

roles.why: The sign t ≥ 0 makes every off-diagonal matrix element nonpositive, which the comparison and Perron-Frobenius both need.
With one hole and no double occupancy, the states are labelled by the hole position and the spins, and the hole moves by hops.
Connectivity is the irreducibility that Perron-Frobenius needs in each spin sector.

steps.slogan: Replace infinite repulsion by the hopping operator projected onto singly occupied states.
steps.detail: Eigenstates with bounded energy as $U \to \infty$ lie in $\ker H_{\mathrm{int}}$ in the limit, and there the Schrödinger equation becomes $E\Phi = P_0 H_{\mathrm{hop}}\Phi$.

steps.slogan: Label states by the hole position and the spins, with signs that make every hop cost $-t_{x,y}$.
steps.detail: With $\Phi_{x,\sigma} = c_{x,\uparrow}\prod_y c^\dagger_{y,\sigma'_y}\Phi_{\mathrm{vac}}$, built with [creation and annihilation operators](c:creation-and-annihilation-operators), the element between different states is $-t_{x,y}$ if the electron at $y$ hops into the hole at $x$, and $0$ otherwise. Diagonal elements do not depend on the spins.

steps.slogan: A ferromagnetic state built from hole amplitudes has energy at most the ground energy.
steps.detail: From a real ground state $\sum \varphi(x,\sigma)\Phi_{x,\sigma}$ put $\xi_x = (\sum_\sigma \varphi(x,\sigma)^2)^{1/2}$ and $\Phi_\uparrow = \sum_x \xi_x \Phi_{x,(\uparrow)}$. Cauchy-Schwarz over $\sigma$ for each pair $x \ne y$ gives $\langle \Phi_\uparrow, \tilde H \Phi_\uparrow\rangle \le \langle \Phi_{GS}, \tilde H \Phi_{GS}\rangle$ with equal norms.

steps.slogan: A connected real symmetric matrix with nonpositive off-diagonal entries has a simple lowest [eigenvalue](c:eigenvalue).
steps.detail: Replacing a lowest eigenvector $v$ by $(|v_i|)$ does not raise the quadratic form, a nonnegative eigenvector is positive by connectivity, and two positive vectors are never orthogonal.

steps.slogan: Each spin sector has one ground state, and it must be the ferromagnetic copy.
steps.detail: $\tilde H$ commutes with $S^{(3)}_{\mathrm{tot}}$ of the [SU(2)](c:su-2) symmetry. In each sector the matrix satisfies the Perron-Frobenius conditions, so its ground state is unique, and the $S_{\max}$ multiplet supplies a ground state in every sector.

concepts.c:ground-state: The conclusion identifies all ground states of the projected hopping operator.
concepts.c:nonnegative-matrix: The hopping matrix has nonnegative entries, which fixes the sign of every hop.
concepts.c:self-adjoint-operator: The infinite repulsion limit is the self-adjoint operator P0 Hhop on singly occupied states.
concepts.c:irreducible-matrix: The connectivity condition says the matrix of each spin sector is irreducible.
concepts.c:creation-and-annihilation-operators: The hole basis is written with fermion creation and annihilation operators to fix the signs.
concepts.c:eigenvalue: Perron-Frobenius gives a simple lowest eigenvalue in each spin sector.

statement: For the nearest-neighbour [Ising model](c:ising-model) on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with $d \ge 5$, the renormalized coupling constant $g(\beta)$, built from the four-point [cumulant](c:cumulant), satisfies $0 \le -g(\beta) \le 2\chi(\beta)^2/\xi(\beta)^d$ and tends to $0$ as $\beta$ increases to the [critical](c:critical-temperature) value.

hypotheses.text: The [Ising model](c:ising-model) is ferromagnetic, nearest-neighbour, with zero field and free boundary conditions in the infinite-volume limit.
The dimension satisfies $d \ge 5$.
The [inverse temperature](c:inverse-temperature) satisfies $0 < \beta < \beta_c$, and $\beta$ increases to $\beta_c$.

conclusion: $0 \le -g(\beta) \le 2\chi(\beta)^2/\xi(\beta)^d$ for $\beta < \beta_c$, and $g(\beta) \to 0$ as $\beta \nearrow \beta_c$.

proofs.name: Random current tree diagram bound
proofs.slogan: Write the four-point cumulant as an intersection probability of random currents, bound it by a tree diagram, and count dimensions with the infrared bound.
proofs.scope: Outline of parts 1 to 6 of Exercise 61 in Duminil-Copin (2017), which follow Aizenman (1982). The monotonicity of cluster intersections and the infrared bound are cited.

roles.why: The random current representation and the switching lemma exist for the Ising model.
The final bound decays like a negative power of the correlation length only when d is at least 5.
Below the critical point the correlations decay exponentially, so the susceptibility and correlation length are finite.

steps.slogan: Express the four-point cumulant as an intersection probability of two [random currents](c:random-current).
steps.detail: The switching lemma gives $U_4 = -2\mu[\sigma_1\sigma_2]\mu[\sigma_3\sigma_4]\,P^{x_1x_2}\otimes P^{x_3x_4}[x_1,\dots,x_4 \text{ all connected}]$, so $U_4 \le 0$.

steps.slogan: Compute the probability that a current with sources $x_1, x_2$ reaches $y$.
steps.detail: Switching with sources $\{x_1,y\}$ and $\{y,x_2\}$ gives $P^{x_1x_2}\otimes P^\emptyset[x_1 \leftrightarrow y] = \mu[\sigma_1\sigma_y]\mu[\sigma_y\sigma_2]/\mu[\sigma_1\sigma_2]$.

steps.slogan: Bound the intersection probability by a tree diagram of four [correlation functions](c:correlation-function).
steps.detail: Two extra sourceless currents make the two clusters independent and can only raise the intersection probability. The union bound over a common point $y$ gives $-U_4 \le 2\sum_y \prod_{i=1}^4 \mu[\sigma_y\sigma_i]$.

steps.slogan: Sum the tree diagram over three points to get $2\chi^4$.
steps.detail: Each sum over $x_i$ gives $\chi(\beta)$ by translation invariance, so $0 \le -g(\beta) \le 2\chi^4/(\chi^2\xi^d) = 2\chi^2/\xi^d$.

steps.slogan: Bound the susceptibility by $C\xi^2(\log\xi)^2$ with exponential decay and the infrared bound.
steps.detail: Griffiths and Messager-Miracle-Solé give $\mu[\sigma_0\sigma_x] \le e^{-\|x\|_\infty/\xi}$. The infrared bound compares the two-point function with the [Green function](c:green-function), so it is at most $C\|x\|^{2-d}$. Splitting the sum at $\|x\|_\infty = 2d\,\xi\log\xi$ gives the bound.

steps.slogan: Let the correlation length diverge and read off $g \to 0$ for $d \ge 5$.
steps.detail: At $\beta_c$ the two-point function is at least $c\|x\|^{1-d}$, so $\chi(\beta) \to \infty$ and $\xi(\beta) \to \infty$. Then $-g \le 2C^2\xi^{4-d}(\log\xi)^4 \to 0$, the [Gaussian](c:gaussian-measure) value.

new_concepts.name: critical temperature
new_concepts.reminder: The critical temperature $T_c=1/(k_B\beta_c)$ separates the disordered phase at high temperature from the ordered phase at low temperature.
new_concepts.definition: The critical temperature $T_c$ of a spin model is the temperature at which the model passes from a disordered phase, with a unique [Gibbs measure](c:gibbs-measure), to an ordered phase. For the [Ising model](c:ising-model) at $h=0$, the critical inverse temperature is $\beta_c=\inf\{\beta\ge0:m^*(\beta)>0\}$, where $m^*$ is the [spontaneous magnetization](c:spontaneous-magnetization), and $T_c=1/(k_B\beta_c)$.

new_concepts.name: free energy
new_concepts.reminder: The free energy is $-1/\beta$ times the pressure $\psi=\lim|\Lambda|^{-1}\log Z_\Lambda$ of a lattice model.
new_concepts.definition: For a lattice spin model with [partition function](c:partition-function) $Z_\Lambda(\beta)$ in a finite box $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^d$, the pressure is the [thermodynamic limit](c:thermodynamic-limit) $\psi(\beta)=\lim_{\Lambda\uparrow\mathbb Z^d}|\Lambda|^{-1}\log Z_\Lambda(\beta)$. The free energy per site is $f(\beta)=-\psi(\beta)/\beta$, where $\beta$ is the [inverse temperature](c:inverse-temperature). For finite-range interactions, the limit exists along boxes, it does not depend on the boundary condition, and $\psi$ is convex.

new_concepts.name: Gibbs measure
new_concepts.reminder: A Gibbs measure is an infinite-volume law whose conditional law in each finite box is the finite Gibbs distribution.
new_concepts.definition: For finite $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^d$ and a [boundary condition](c:boundary-condition) $\eta$, let $\pi_\Lambda^\eta$ be the finite-volume [Gibbs distribution](c:gibbs-distribution) of an interaction in $\Lambda$, with the spins outside $\Lambda$ fixed to $\eta$. A [probability measure](c:probability-measure) $\mu$ on the configuration space $S^{\mathbb Z^d}$ is a Gibbs measure if, for every finite $\Lambda$, the [conditional distribution](c:conditional-distribution) of the spins in $\Lambda$ given the spins outside $\Lambda$ is $\pi_\Lambda^\eta$ for $\mu$-almost every outside configuration $\eta$. These conditions are the DLR equations.

new_concepts.name: Green function
new_concepts.reminder: The Green function $G(x,y)$ counts the expected visits to $y$ of a random walk from $x$ before it is killed.
new_concepts.definition: For simple [random walk](c:random-walk) $(X_n)$ on $\mathbb Z^d$ and a finite set $\Lambda$, with exit time $\tau=\min\{n\ge0:X_n\notin\Lambda\}$, the Green function is $G_\Lambda(x,y)=\mathbb E_x\big[\sum_{n=0}^{\tau-1}\mathbf 1\{X_n=y\}\big]$. As a matrix, $G_\Lambda=(I-P_\Lambda)^{-1}$, where $P_\Lambda$ is the transition matrix restricted to $\Lambda$, so $G_\Lambda$ inverts the killed [discrete Laplacian](c:discrete-laplace-operator) $-\frac1{2d}\Delta$. For a transient walk one can take $\Lambda=\mathbb Z^d$, and then $G(x,y)=\sum_{n\ge0}P^n(x,y)$.

new_concepts.name: inverse temperature
new_concepts.reminder: The inverse temperature $\beta=1/(k_BT)$ multiplies the energy in the Boltzmann weight $e^{-\beta H}$.
new_concepts.definition: The inverse temperature of a system at absolute temperature $T$ is $\beta=1/(k_BT)$, where $k_B$ is Boltzmann's constant. It is the parameter in the [Boltzmann distribution](c:boltzmann-distribution) $\mu_\beta(\sigma)=e^{-\beta H(\sigma)}/Z(\beta)$ of a [Hamiltonian](c:hamiltonian) $H$. Mathematical texts usually set $k_B=1$ and use $\beta\in[0,\infty)$ as the parameter.

new_concepts.name: phase transition
new_concepts.reminder: A phase transition is a parameter value where the infinite-volume free energy is not analytic or several Gibbs measures coexist.
new_concepts.definition: A phase transition of a lattice model is a value of its parameters, such as the inverse temperature $\beta$ and the field $h$, at which the infinite-volume [free energy](c:free-energy) is not real-analytic. It is first-order when a first derivative of the free energy is discontinuous there. In the [Ising model](c:ising-model) this happens at $h=0$ and $\beta>\beta_c$, where the derivative in $h$ jumps and several infinite-volume [Gibbs measures](c:gibbs-measure) coexist.

new_concepts.name: random current
new_concepts.reminder: A random current is a random integer-valued function on edges whose odd-degree vertices form a prescribed source set.
new_concepts.definition: For the [Ising model](c:ising-model) on a finite graph $G=(V,E)$ with coupling constants $\beta J_{xy}\ge0$, a current is a function $n:E\to\{0,1,2,\dots\}$, and its source set $\partial n$ is the set of vertices $x$ with $\sum_yn_{xy}$ odd. The weight of $n$ is $w(n)=\prod_{xy\in E}(\beta J_{xy})^{n_{xy}}/n_{xy}!$, and the random current with sources $A$ has law proportional to $w(n)\mathbf 1\{\partial n=A\}$. Expanding each factor $e^{\beta J_{xy}\sigma_x\sigma_y}$ in a power series gives $\langle\prod_{x\in A}\sigma_x\rangle=\sum_{\partial n=A}w(n)/\sum_{\partial n=\emptyset}w(n)$.

new_concepts.name: spontaneous magnetization
new_concepts.reminder: The spontaneous magnetization $m^*(\beta)=\lim_{h\downarrow0}\langle\sigma_0\rangle_{\beta,h}$ is the magnetization that remains when the external field vanishes.
new_concepts.definition: For the [Ising model](c:ising-model) on $\mathbb Z^d$ at [inverse temperature](c:inverse-temperature) $\beta$, the spontaneous magnetization is $m^*(\beta)=\lim_{h\downarrow0}\langle\sigma_0\rangle_{\beta,h}$, where $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\beta,h}$ is the infinite-volume state in the field $h>0$. It equals $\langle\sigma_0\rangle^+_\beta$, the [expected value](c:expected-value) of the spin at the origin under the plus Gibbs measure at $h=0$, and also the right derivative $\partial\psi/\partial h(\beta,0^+)$ of the pressure. For $d\ge2$, $m^*(\beta)=0$ for $\beta\le\beta_c$ and $m^*(\beta)>0$ for $\beta>\beta_c$.

statement: In dimension $4$, smeared averages of the nearest-neighbour [Ising model](c:ising-model) and of the lattice [phi^4 model](c:phi4-model) at or below the [critical](c:critical-temperature) point have a [characteristic function](c:characteristic-function) within $C z^4/(\log L)^c$ of a Gaussian one, so every scaling limit is a [Gaussian process](c:gaussian-process).

hypotheses.text: The dimension is $d = 4$ and the coupling is nearest-neighbour and ferromagnetic.
The single-site law is in the Griffiths-Simon class, which contains the [Ising model](c:ising-model) spin and the [phi^4 model](c:phi4-model) measures.
The [inverse temperature](c:inverse-temperature) satisfies $\beta \le \beta_c$ and the scale satisfies $2 \le L \le \xi(\beta)$.

conclusion: $|\langle \exp[zT_{f,L} - \tfrac{z^2}{2}\langle T_{f,L}^2\rangle]\rangle - 1| \le C\|f\|_\infty^4 r_f^{12} z^4/(\log L)^c$ for all real $z$, and every scaling limit with vanishing two-point function at infinity is a generalized Gaussian process.

proofs.name: Improved tree diagram bound by multi-scale random current analysis
proofs.slogan: Current clusters that intersect in four dimensions intersect on many scales, which gains a power of the bubble diagram over the tree diagram bound.
proofs.scope: Outline of Aizenman and Duminil-Copin (2021), Sections 3 to 7. The regularity, intersection and mixing estimates are cited from the source.

roles.why: In four dimensions the bubble diagram grows like log L, and the mixing proof needs d at least 4.
Griffiths-Simon variables are block averages of Ising spins, so the random current tools apply to them.
Regular scales and mixing are available only up to the correlation length.

steps.slogan: Bound the four-point [cumulant](c:cumulant) by the probability that two [random current](c:random-current) clusters intersect.
steps.detail: The switching lemma and a monotonicity give $|U_4| \le 2\langle\sigma_x\sigma_y\rangle\langle\sigma_z\sigma_t\rangle P[T \ne \emptyset]$ with $T = C_{n_1+n_3}(x) \cap C_{n_2+n_4}(z)$. The first moment of $|T|$ gives only the tree diagram bound.

steps.slogan: Find many regular scales on which the two-point function behaves like a power law.
steps.detail: The infrared bound, its sliding-scale form and the Messager-Miracle-Solé monotonicity show that at least $c\log_2(N/n)$ scales between $n$ and $N \le \xi$ are regular.

steps.slogan: Show that clusters cross each annulus once and intersect there with probability at least $c$.
steps.detail: A second moment bound on the number of intersection points in an annulus gives $P[M \ne \emptyset] \ge (E|M|)^2/E|M|^2 \ge c$ when the source lies in a regular scale.

steps.slogan: Prove that random currents in distant annuli are nearly independent.
steps.detail: Theorem 6.4 of the source gives $|P[E\cap F] - P[E]P[F]| \le s(\log(N/n))^{-c}$ for events inside $\Lambda_n$ and outside $\Lambda_N$ with $n^\alpha \le N \le \xi$.

steps.slogan: Combine intersection and mixing to get many intersecting annuli and the improved tree diagram bound.
steps.detail: Except with probability $2^{-\delta K}$ the clusters meet in at least $\delta K$ annuli around $u$. A covering lemma, the union bound and Markov's inequality give $|U_4| \le C B_L^{-c}\sum_u \prod_i\langle\sigma_u\sigma_{x_i}\rangle$.

steps.slogan: Turn the four-point bound into a bound on the characteristic function of smeared spins.
steps.detail: Aizenman's inequality bounds the deviation of every $2n$-point function from Wick's rule by $U_4$ terms. Summing the moment bounds with $z^{2n}/(2n)!$ and estimating the sum $S(L,r,\beta)$ gives the factor $(\log L)^{-c}$.

steps.slogan: Extend the bound to the Griffiths-Simon class and conclude Gaussianity of every scaling limit.
steps.detail: Block averages of Ising spins and their weak limits include $\phi^4$, the bounds are uniform in $\rho$, and a characteristic function close to a Gaussian one gives a [Gaussian process](c:gaussian-process) in the limit.

statement: On the two-dimensional torus, the Boltzmann weight $e^{-G}$ of the [Wick ordered](c:renormalization) [phi^4 model](c:phi4-model) interaction $G = \frac{1}{2m}\int :|u|^{2m}:\,dx$, $m \ge 2$, is in every $L^p$ of the [Gaussian free field](c:gaussian-free-field), and the cut-off weights $e^{-G_N}$ converge to it in $L^p$.

hypotheses.text: The field has the law $\mu$ of the [Gaussian free field](c:gaussian-free-field) on the torus with covariance $(1-\Delta)^{-1}$.
The interaction is a [Wick ordered](c:renormalization) power $\frac{1}{2m}\int :|u_N|^{2m}:\,dx$ with $m \ge 2$ and a positive sign.
The torus has dimension $2$, so $\sigma_N = E|u_N(x)|^2$ grows only like $\log N$.

conclusion: For every finite $p$, $\sup_N \|e^{-G_N}\|_{L^p(\mu)} < \infty$ and $e^{-G_N} \to e^{-G}$ in $L^p(\mu)$, so the [partition function](c:partition-function) $Z = \int e^{-G}\,d\mu$ is finite and positive.

proofs.name: Nelson's argument: hypercontractive tails against a logarithmic lower bound
proofs.slogan: The interaction is below its mean by at most a power of log N, and deviations of that size have super-exponentially small probability.
proofs.scope: Outline of Oh and Thomann (2018), Sections 2.2 to 2.4. The Wiener chaos estimate is cited, not proved.

roles.why: Gaussianity gives the orthogonality of Wick powers and the hypercontractive moment bounds.
Wick ordering makes the cut-off interactions converge, and the positive sign gives the lower bound.
In two dimensions the variance is logarithmic, so the lower bound is only a power of log N.

steps.slogan: Write the Wick power with a [Hermite polynomial](c:hermite-polynomial) or a Laguerre polynomial.
steps.detail: With $u_N(x) = \sigma_N^{1/2} W_{\eta_N(x)}$ and a unit vector $\eta_N(x)$, the Wick power is $\sigma_N^m$ times a fixed polynomial of a standard Gaussian variable.

steps.slogan: Show that the cut-off interactions form a Cauchy sequence in $L^2$.
steps.detail: Orthogonality of the polynomials gives $\|G_M - G_N\|^2_{L^2}$ as an integral of $\gamma_M^{2m} - \gamma_N^{2m}$, which is at most $C_m/N$.

steps.slogan: Upgrade the $L^2$ bound to stretched exponential tails by hypercontractivity.
steps.detail: Polynomials of degree $2m$ satisfy $\|F\|_{L^p} \le (p-1)^m \|F\|_{L^2}$, and Markov's inequality with an optimal $p$ gives $\mu(|G_M - G_N| > \lambda) \le C e^{-c N^{1/(2m)} \lambda^{1/m}}$.

steps.slogan: Bound $-G_N$ from above by a power of $\log N$.
steps.detail: The Wick polynomial is bounded below by $-a_m \sigma_N^m$ and $\sigma_N \le C\log N$, so $-G_N \le b_m (\log N)^m$ for every field.

steps.slogan: Compare $G_N$ with a coarser cut-off $G_{N_0}$ chosen for each level $\lambda$.
steps.detail: With $\lambda = 2pb_m(\log N_0)^m$, the event $-pG_N > \lambda$ is empty for $N < N_0$ and forces a deviation $p|G_N - G_{N_0}| > \lambda/2$ for $N \ge N_0$, whose probability is far below $e^{-(1+\delta)\lambda}$.

steps.slogan: Combine uniform bounds with convergence in measure to get $L^p$ convergence of the weights.
steps.detail: Convergence in measure and uniform $L^{2p}$ bounds give $e^{-G_N} \to e^{-G}$ in $L^p$ by the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, and $e^{-G} > 0$ gives $Z > 0$.

concepts.c:renormalization: Wick ordering subtracts the divergent self-contractions of the power.
concepts.c:phi4-model: For m = 2 the interaction is the phi^4 interaction in two dimensions.

concepts.c:hermite-polynomial: Hermite polynomials define the Wick powers of a real field.

statement: For every coupling $\lambda > 0$ and mass $m^2 \in \mathbb{R}$, suitably [renormalized](c:renormalization) lattice [phi^4 model](c:phi4-model) measures on $(\varepsilon\mathbb{Z}/M\mathbb{Z})^3$ are [tight](c:tightness) as $\varepsilon \to 0$ and $M \to \infty$, and every limit is translation invariant, [reflection positive](c:reflection-positivity), non-Gaussian and has stretched exponential moments.

hypotheses.text: The coupling is $\lambda > 0$ and the mass parameter $m^2$ is any real number.
The approximations are the lattice [Gibbs measures](c:gibbs-measure) of the [phi^4 model](c:phi4-model) with mass counterterm $-3\lambda a_{M,\varepsilon} + 3\lambda^2 b_{M,\varepsilon}$.
The lattice fields are extended to [tempered distributions](c:tempered-distribution) on $\mathbb{R}^3$ and the limit $\varepsilon \to 0$, $M \to \infty$ is taken along subsequences.

conclusion: The family is tight on $\mathcal{S}'(\mathbb{R}^3)$, and every accumulation point $\nu$ is translation invariant, reflection positive, non-Gaussian, satisfies $\int \exp\{\beta\|(1+|\cdot|^2)^{-\sigma}\phi\|^{1-\upsilon}_{H^{-1/2-\kappa}}\}\,d\nu < \infty$ and satisfies the Dyson-Schwinger equations.

proofs.name: Stochastic quantization and a paracontrolled energy method
proofs.slogan: Realize each lattice measure as the invariant law of a stochastic heat equation, and bound the stationary solution uniformly by a renormalized energy estimate.
proofs.scope: Outline of Gubinelli and Hofmanová (2021), Sections 3 to 6. The stochastic estimates and the paraproduct lemmas are cited from the source.

roles.why: The energy estimate needs the quartic term with lambda > 0, and non-Gaussianity comes from the term of order lambda.
The counterterms cancel the divergent Wick ordering and second order terms in the dynamics.
Tightness and the passage to the limit take place in weighted spaces of distributions on R^3.

steps.slogan: Write each lattice measure as the [invariant measure](c:invariant-measure) of a stochastic heat equation.
steps.detail: The gradient-form equation $\partial_t\phi + (m^2 - \Delta_\varepsilon)\phi + \lambda\phi^3 + (-3\lambda a + 3\lambda^2 b)\phi = \xi$ driven by lattice [white noise](c:white-noise) has $\nu_{M,\varepsilon}$ as invariant law, so a stationary solution has law $\nu_{M,\varepsilon}$ at every time.

steps.slogan: Split the field into the free field, a fixed-point term and a more regular remainder.
steps.detail: Write $\phi = X + Y + \varphi$, where $X$ is the Gaussian solution, $Y$ cancels the Wick cube and a paraproduct by a Banach fixed point, and $\varphi$ solves an equation with only controllable products.

steps.slogan: Test the remainder equation with the remainder and complete the square with a paracontrolled ansatz.
steps.detail: The resonant and paraproduct terms nearly coincide inside the duality pairing, and the ansatz $\psi$ absorbs them. Young's inequality gives a bound on $\|\rho^2\varphi\|^2_{L^2}$, $\lambda\|\rho\varphi\|^4_{L^4}$ and $\|\rho^2\varphi\|^2_{H^{1-2\kappa}}$ uniform in $M$ and $\varepsilon$.

steps.slogan: Use stationarity to turn the energy bound into uniform moments, then into tightness.
steps.detail: Averaging in time gives $E\|\phi\|^{2p}_{H^{-1/2-2\kappa}(\rho^2)} \lesssim 1 + \lambda^{3p}$, and a compact embedding with Prokhorov's theorem gives limit points with the same bounds.

steps.slogan: Pass translation invariance, [reflection positivity](c:reflection-positivity) and exponential moments to the limit.
steps.detail: Lattice shifts approximate every shift, a cut-off near the reflection plane makes the lattice reflection positivity applicable, and a refined energy bound gives stretched exponential moments and the axiom OS0.

steps.slogan: Show that the connected four-point function is negative at high momenta.
steps.detail: With $\phi = X - \lambda\mathbb{X} + \zeta$ the four-point [cumulant](c:cumulant) of a Littlewood-Paley block is $-4\lambda L(X,X,X,\mathbb{X}) + R$, of order $-\lambda 2^i$, since $|R| \lesssim 2^{i(1/2+5\kappa)}$.

steps.slogan: Collect the properties of every accumulation point and add the integration by parts formula.
steps.detail: Every limit point has the properties of the two previous steps, and a second paracontrolled ansatz identifies the renormalized cube and gives the Dyson-Schwinger equations.

concepts.c:renormalization: The lattice measures carry two mass counterterms that diverge as the mesh tends to 0.
concepts.c:phi4-model: The construction is the continuum limit of the lattice phi^4 model in three dimensions.
concepts.c:tightness: Tightness of the lattice measures gives limit points in the space of distributions.
concepts.c:reflection-positivity: Reflection positivity of the limit is the Osterwalder-Schrader positivity axiom.
concepts.c:gibbs-measure: Each approximation is a finite-volume Gibbs measure on the periodic lattice.
concepts.c:tempered-distribution: The limit field is a random tempered distribution, not a function.
concepts.c:invariant-measure: Each lattice measure is the invariant measure of its stochastic quantization equation.
concepts.c:white-noise: Space-time white noise drives the stochastic quantization equation.
concepts.c:cumulant: Non-Gaussianity is proved by showing that the fourth cumulant is not 0.

new_concepts.name: Gaussian free field
new_concepts.reminder: The Gaussian free field is the centered Gaussian field whose covariance is the Green function of the Laplacian.
new_concepts.definition: The discrete Gaussian free field on a finite set $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^d$ with zero boundary values is the centered Gaussian vector $(\varphi_x)_{x\in\Lambda}$ with covariance $\mathbb E[\varphi_x\varphi_y]=G_\Lambda(x,y)$, the [Green function](c:green-function) of simple random walk killed when it leaves $\Lambda$. Its density is proportional to $\exp\big(-\frac1{4d}\sum_{x\sim y}(\varphi_x-\varphi_y)^2\big)$, with $\varphi=0$ outside $\Lambda$. In the continuum, the Gaussian free field is the centered Gaussian random distribution whose covariance is the Green function of the Dirichlet Laplacian.

new_concepts.name: Gibbs measure
new_concepts.reminder: A Gibbs measure is an infinite-volume law whose conditional law in each finite box is the finite Gibbs distribution.
new_concepts.definition: For finite $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^d$ and a [boundary condition](c:boundary-condition) $\eta$, let $\pi_\Lambda^\eta$ be the finite-volume [Gibbs distribution](c:gibbs-distribution) of an interaction in $\Lambda$, with the spins outside $\Lambda$ fixed to $\eta$. A [probability measure](c:probability-measure) $\mu$ on the configuration space $S^{\mathbb Z^d}$ is a Gibbs measure if, for every finite $\Lambda$, the [conditional distribution](c:conditional-distribution) of the spins in $\Lambda$ given the spins outside $\Lambda$ is $\pi_\Lambda^\eta$ for $\mu$-almost every outside configuration $\eta$. These conditions are the DLR equations.

new_concepts.name: Green function
new_concepts.reminder: The Green function $G(x,y)$ counts the expected visits to $y$ of a random walk from $x$ before it is killed.
new_concepts.definition: For simple [random walk](c:random-walk) $(X_n)$ on $\mathbb Z^d$ and a finite set $\Lambda$, with exit time $\tau=\min\{n\ge0:X_n\notin\Lambda\}$, the Green function is $G_\Lambda(x,y)=\mathbb E_x\big[\sum_{n=0}^{\tau-1}\mathbf 1\{X_n=y\}\big]$. As a matrix, $G_\Lambda=(I-P_\Lambda)^{-1}$, where $P_\Lambda$ is the transition matrix restricted to $\Lambda$, so $G_\Lambda$ inverts the killed [discrete Laplacian](c:discrete-laplace-operator) $-\frac1{2d}\Delta$. For a transient walk one can take $\Lambda=\mathbb Z^d$, and then $G(x,y)=\sum_{n\ge0}P^n(x,y)$.

new_concepts.name: phi^4 model
new_concepts.reminder: The $\varphi^4$ model is a lattice field with Gaussian gradient coupling and a quartic potential $\lambda\varphi^4+\mu\varphi^2$ at each site.
new_concepts.definition: The lattice $\varphi^4$ model on a finite set $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^d$ is the probability measure on $\mathbb R^\Lambda$ with density proportional to $\exp\big(-\frac12\sum_{x\sim y}(\varphi_x-\varphi_y)^2-\sum_{x\in\Lambda}(\lambda\varphi_x^4+\mu\varphi_x^2)\big)$ with respect to [Lebesgue measure](c:lebesgue-measure), where $\lambda>0$, $\mu\in\mathbb R$ and $\varphi=0$ outside $\Lambda$. The continuum $\varphi^4_d$ field theory is a limit of such measures with renormalized parameters as the lattice spacing tends to $0$. It exists as a non-Gaussian theory for $d=2,3$, and such limits are Gaussian for $d\ge4$.

statement: In a lattice gauge theory with [compact gauge group](c:compact-group) $G$ at small inverse coupling $\beta$, the [Wilson loop](c:wilson-loop) of an $R \times T$ rectangle, in a representation that is nontrivial on the [center](c:center) of $G$, has expectation at most $2d_\rho\, c_1^{R+T}\delta(\beta)^{RT}$, uniformly in the volume.

hypotheses.text: $G$ is compact with normalized [Haar measure](c:haar-measure), and the action is $\beta\sum_p \operatorname{Re}\chi_\sigma(U_p)$ for a unitary representation $\sigma$ of dimension $n_\sigma$ on a box $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{Z}^d$, $d \ge 2$.
The loop uses an [irreducible representation](c:irreducible-representation) $\rho$ with $\rho(z) \ne I$ for some $z$ in a finite central subgroup $Z$.
$\delta(\beta) = 2eD^2(e^{2\beta n_\sigma} - 1) \le \tfrac12$ with $D = 4(2d-3)$.
$C$ is the boundary of an $R \times T$ rectangle in a coordinate plane inside $\Lambda$, with $R, T \ge 1$.

conclusion: $|\langle W_C\rangle_\Lambda| \le 2d_\rho\, c_1^{R+T}\, \delta(\beta)^{RT}$ with $c_1 = 16^{d-1}e^2$, for every box $\Lambda$ that contains the rectangle.

proofs.name: Polymer expansion with center charges
proofs.slogan: Expand the plaquette weights into polymers, use center symmetry to force the polymers touching the loop to cover the rectangle, and control the rest by cluster expansion.
proofs.scope: The whole theorem for free boundary conditions on boxes. Infinite-volume limits follow because the bound does not depend on the box.

roles.why: Haar measure invariance under central shifts and the bound $|\operatorname{Re}\chi_\sigma| \le n_\sigma$ drive the expansion.
A central element on which $\rho$ is nontrivial gives the nonzero charge $\zeta$ that the polymers must carry.
Small $\delta(\beta)$ makes the cluster expansion converge and the sum over large polymer sets geometric.
A planar rectangle lets the projection onto its plane count one plaquette per enclosed square.

steps.slogan: Write each plaquette weight as $c(\beta)(1+f_p)$ and group plaquettes into [polymers](c:polymer-model).
steps.detail: With $|f_p| \le \varepsilon = e^{2\beta n_\sigma} - 1$, the partition function becomes a polymer gas whose polymers are connected plaquette sets. In the numerator, the components $\Gamma$ that meet the loop factor out as $K(\Gamma) = \int W_C \prod_{p\in\Gamma} f_p\,dU$, so $\langle W_C\rangle = \sum_\Gamma K(\Gamma)\,\Xi(\Gamma)/\Xi$.

steps.slogan: Split each $f_p$ into [center](c:center) charges and shift links by central elements.
steps.detail: Write $f = \sum_\eta f^\eta$ with $f^\eta(zU) = \eta(z) f^\eta(U)$. The substitution $U_e \to zU_e$ preserves [Haar measure](c:haar-measure) and multiplies the integrand by $\zeta(z)^{[C:e]}\prod_p \eta_p(z)^{[p:e]}$, so a nonzero term needs $\partial\eta = -\zeta C$ for the charge chain.

steps.slogan: Project the charge chain onto the plane of the loop to show that it covers the rectangle.
steps.detail: Projection onto the first two coordinates is a [chain map](c:chain-map) for the [boundary operator](c:boundary-operator). A finitely supported planar 2-chain without boundary vanishes, so the projected charge equals $-\zeta$ on each of the $RT$ squares, and $K(\Gamma) = 0$ unless $|\Gamma| \ge RT$.

steps.slogan: Bound the ratio $\Xi(\Gamma)/\Xi$ of polymer partition functions by the [cluster expansion](c:cluster-expansion).
steps.detail: At most $D^{2(n-1)}$ polymers of size $n$ contain a given plaquette, so the Kotecky-Preiss condition holds with $a(\gamma) = |\gamma|$. Excluded polymers meet a plaquette of $\Gamma$ or a square next to $C$, which gives $\Xi(\Gamma)/\Xi \le e^{|\Gamma| + |C|}$.

steps.slogan: Count the polymer sets that touch the loop and sum over sizes at least $RT$.
steps.detail: There are at most $2^M(2D^2)^n$ admissible sets of size $n$ with $M = 2(d-1)|C|$. Each contributes at most $d_\rho\varepsilon^n e^{n + |C|}$, so the geometric sum from $n = RT$ gives $2d_\rho c_1^{R+T}\delta^{RT}$.

concepts.c:compact-group: The gauge group is compact, so its normalized Haar measure exists.
concepts.c:wilson-loop: The Wilson loop is the observable whose expectation the theorem bounds.
concepts.c:center: Central elements act on every plaquette variable by a scalar and give the conserved charge.
concepts.c:haar-measure: Invariance of Haar measure under central shifts makes most charge configurations integrate to zero.
concepts.c:irreducible-representation: Irreducibility lets Schur's lemma make central elements act by the scalar $\zeta(z)$.
concepts.c:polymer-model: The expanded partition function is a gas of connected plaquette sets with small activities.
concepts.c:chain-map: The projection onto the plane of the loop commutes with the boundary operator.
concepts.c:boundary-operator: The charge condition says that the boundary of the charge chain equals the loop.
concepts.c:cluster-expansion: The cluster expansion controls the ratio of the restricted and full polymer partition functions.

source.note: The original proof of Osterwalder and Seiler (Ann. Physics 110, 1978) is not available as an open copy. These steps give a self-contained polymer expansion proof with a center charge argument and explicit constants.

new_concepts.name: cluster expansion
new_concepts.reminder: The cluster expansion writes the logarithm of a polymer partition function as a series over connected clusters of polymers.
new_concepts.definition: For a [polymer model](c:polymer-model) with activities $z(\gamma)$ and partition function $\Xi$, the cluster expansion is the series $\log\Xi=\sum_{n\ge1}\sum_{\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_n}\varphi(\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_n)\prod_{i=1}^nz(\gamma_i)$. The Ursell function is $\varphi(\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_n)=\frac1{n!}\sum_G(-1)^{|E(G)|}$, summed over the connected spanning subgraphs $G$ of the incompatibility graph on $\{1,\dots,n\}$, so only connected clusters contribute. The Kotecký–Preiss condition $\sum_{\gamma'\not\sim\gamma}|z(\gamma')|e^{a(\gamma')}\le a(\gamma)$ for all $\gamma$ makes the series converge absolutely.

new_concepts.name: polymer model
new_concepts.reminder: A polymer model is a gas of polymers with activities, in which incompatible polymers cannot appear together.
new_concepts.definition: An abstract polymer model consists of a countable set $\mathcal P$ of polymers, a symmetric and reflexive incompatibility relation on $\mathcal P$, and an activity $z:\mathcal P\to\mathbb C$. For a finite set of polymers, the polymer [partition function](c:partition-function) is $\Xi=\sum_\Gamma\prod_{\gamma\in\Gamma}z(\gamma)$, summed over all families $\Gamma$ of pairwise compatible polymers, the empty family included.

statement: For a finite weighted graph, the two-point integral of an $n$-component field against $F(\tau)$, with $\tau_x = \tfrac12|\phi_x|^2$ and weight $e^{-\frac12(\phi,-\Delta_\beta\phi)}$, equals the same field integral of the [local time](c:local-time) expectation $\int_0^\infty E_x[F(\tau + L_T)\,1\{X(T)=y\}]\,dT$ of the [random walk](c:random-walk) with generator $\Delta_\beta$.

hypotheses.text: $\Lambda$ is finite, $\beta_{xy} = \beta_{yx} \ge 0$, and $X$ is the continuous-time [Markov chain](c:markov-chain) that jumps from $x$ to $y$ at rate $\beta_{xy}$.
$F$ is a Borel function on $[0,\infty)^\Lambda$ with $|F(t)| \le C e^{-\varepsilon \sum_z t_z}$ for some $C$ and $\varepsilon > 0$.

conclusion: $\int e^{-\frac12(\phi,-\Delta_\beta\phi)} F(\tau)\,\phi^1_x\phi^1_y\,d\phi = \int e^{-\frac12(\phi,-\Delta_\beta\phi)} \int_0^\infty E_x[F(\tau+L_T)\,1\{X(T)=y\}]\,dT\,d\phi$, and both integrals converge absolutely.

proofs.name: Exponential case and Laplace uniqueness
proofs.slogan: Prove the identity for exponentials, where both sides equal a Green function times a Gaussian integral, then extend it by uniqueness of Laplace transforms.
proofs.scope: The whole theorem, for every $n \ge 1$, every pair $x, y$ and every Borel $F$ with the exponential bound. The steps follow the source for the exponential case and replace its Fourier inversion by a Laplace uniqueness argument.

roles.why: Symmetric nonnegative weights make $-\Delta_\beta + V$ positive definite and make the walk a Markov chain with a first-jump equation.
The exponential bound makes both sides absolutely convergent and lets a weight $e^{-\delta\sum t}$ define finite measures.

steps.slogan: Compute the [Gaussian integral](c:gaussian-integral) of $\phi^1_x\phi^1_y$ with a positive mass $V$.
steps.detail: For $A = -\Delta_\beta + V$ with $v_z > 0$, the form $(u, Au) \ge \min v\,|u|^2$ is positive definite, and $e^{-\frac12(\phi,-\Delta_\beta\phi)}e^{-(v,\tau)} = e^{-\frac12(\phi,A\phi)}$. Each component is centred Gaussian with covariance $A^{-1}$, so the two-point integral equals $(A^{-1})_{xy} Z_A$.

steps.slogan: Show that the killed walk resolvent is the [Green function](c:green-function) $(-\Delta_\beta + V)^{-1}$.
steps.detail: Set $G(x,y) = \int_0^\infty E_x[e^{-\sum_u v_u L_{T,u}} 1\{X(T)=y\}]\,dT$. Splitting at the first jump time, which is exponential with rate $\bar\beta_x$, and the strong Markov property give $(\bar\beta_x + v_x)G(x,y) - \sum_{z \ne x}\beta_{xz}G(z,y) = \delta_{xy}$, that is $AG = I$.

steps.slogan: Verify the identity for exponential test functions $F(t) = e^{-(v,t)}$ with $v > 0$.
steps.detail: The factor $e^{-(v,\tau+L_T)}$ splits into a field part and a walk part. Tonelli's theorem makes the right side $Z_A\,G(x,y)$, and the two previous steps show that both sides equal $(A^{-1})_{xy} Z_A$.

steps.slogan: Encode both sides as finite [signed measures](c:signed-measure) on the orthant with equal [Laplace transforms](c:laplace-transform).
steps.detail: With $\delta = \varepsilon/2$, push the weighted field measure forward by $\tau$ to get $\mu_L$, and push the weighted field and walk measure forward by $\tau + L_T$ to get $\mu_R$. Both are finite because $\sum_u L_{T,u} = T$. Their Laplace transforms at $w \ge 0$ are the two sides for $F = e^{-(w+\delta,t)}$, so they agree.

steps.slogan: Exponential functions are dense on the compactified orthant, so the two measures coincide.
steps.detail: On $K = [0,\infty]^\Lambda$ the span of $e^{-(w,t)}$ is an algebra with constants that separates points. Stone-Weierstrass makes it dense in $C(K)$, so the measures agree on $C(K)$, and the uniqueness in the Riesz-Markov-Kakutani theorem gives $\mu_L = \mu_R$.

steps.slogan: Integrate the bounded function $F(t)e^{\delta\sum t_z}$ against the two equal measures.
steps.detail: The function $H = F e^{\delta \sum_z t_z}$ is bounded and Borel. Its integral against $\mu_L$ is the left side for $F$, and its integral against $\mu_R$ is the right side, because the weights cancel. The equality $\mu_L = \mu_R$ gives the theorem.

concepts.c:local-time: The local time field of the walk is the random shift that appears in $F(\tau + L_T)$.
concepts.c:random-walk: The continuous-time random walk with rates $\beta_{xy}$ supplies the right side of the identity.
concepts.c:markov-chain: The walk is a continuous-time Markov chain, which gives the first-jump equation for the resolvent.
concepts.c:gaussian-integral: The exponential case reduces to a Gaussian integral with covariance $(-\Delta_\beta+V)^{-1}$.
concepts.c:green-function: The walk resolvent equals the Green function $(-\Delta_\beta+V)^{-1}$, which is the Gaussian covariance.
concepts.c:signed-measure: Both sides of the identity define finite signed measures on the orthant.
concepts.c:laplace-transform: Equal Laplace transforms of the two measures carry the identity from exponentials to all $F$.

source.ref: R. Bauerschmidt, D. C. Brydges and G. Slade, Introduction to a Renormalisation Group Method (Springer LNM 2242, 2019), Lemma 11.2.2 and Theorem 11.2.3, pp. 176-178.

new_concepts.name: local time
new_concepts.reminder: The local time $L_t^x$ measures how much time a process spends near the level $x$ up to time $t$.
new_concepts.definition: For a one-dimensional [Brownian motion](c:brownian-motion) $B$, the local time is the jointly continuous process $(L_t^x)_{t\ge0,x\in\mathbb{R}}$ such that $\int_0^tf(B_s)\,ds=\int_{\mathbb{R}}f(x)L_t^x\,dx$ for all bounded Borel functions $f$ and all $t$, almost surely. So $x\mapsto L_t^x$ is the [Radon–Nikodym derivative](c:radon-nikodym-derivative) of the occupation measure $A\mapsto\int_0^t1_A(B_s)\,ds$ with respect to [Lebesgue measure](c:lebesgue-measure). For a continuous [semimartingale](c:semimartingale) $X$, the same formula with $d\langle X\rangle_s$ in place of $ds$ defines $L_t^x$, which is then right-continuous in $x$.

statement: For a [Markov chain](c:markov-chain) on a finite graph, started at $x_0$ and stopped when its [local time](c:local-time) at $x_0$ exceeds $u$, the local times plus $\frac12\phi^2$ for an independent [Gaussian free field](c:gaussian-free-field) $\phi$ pinned at $x_0$ have the same law as $\frac12(\phi + \sqrt{2u})^2$.

hypotheses.text: The graph is finite and connected with positive symmetric conductances, and the [Markov chain](c:markov-chain) jumps along edges at rates given by the conductances.
The field $\phi$ is the [Gaussian free field](c:gaussian-free-field) with $\phi_{x_0} = 0$, independent of the chain.
The chain starts at $x_0$ and the [local time](c:local-time) is read at $\tau_u = \inf\{t : \ell_{x_0}(t) > u\}$.

conclusion: $\left(\ell_x(\tau_u) + \tfrac12\phi_x^2\right)_{x\in V}$ has the same law as $\left(\tfrac12(\phi_x + \sqrt{2u})^2\right)_{x\in V}$.

proofs.name: Change of variables and a spin-flip martingale
proofs.slogan: Change variables to the square roots of local time plus half the field squared, and show that the Jacobian factor is a martingale whose bad terms cancel by flipping signs.
proofs.scope: Outline of Sabot and Tarrès (2016), Section 2. The martingale property of the Feynman-Kac type functional is cited.

roles.why: A finite connected graph makes every local time grow without bound, so the stopping time is finite, and it gives the Dirichlet form.
The Gaussian density of the field is the weight that the change of variables transports.
Stopping at the inverse local time fixes the value at x_0 to the square root of 2u.

steps.slogan: Write the field as signs times absolute values and sum over the sign vectors.
steps.detail: The Gaussian integral over $\mathbb{R}^U$ becomes a sum over $\sigma \in \{\pm1\}^V$ with $\sigma_{x_0} = 1$ of integrals over the positive quadrant with weight $e^{-\mathcal{E}(\sigma\phi,\sigma\phi)/2}$.

steps.slogan: Substitute $\Phi = (2\ell(\tau_u) + \phi^2)^{1/2}$ and read the result at the first time a local time reaches $\Phi^2/2$.
steps.detail: The Jacobian is $\prod_{x\in U}\Phi_x/\phi_x$, and $\Phi$ is in the image exactly when the [stopping time](c:stopping-time) $T$ is $\tau_u$ and $X_T = x_0$.

steps.slogan: Show that the transported density is a [martingale](c:martingale) in time.
steps.detail: Along the path only $\Phi_{X_t}(t)$ moves, and the derivative of the energy equals $2\tilde L f/f$ for a product function $f$, which gives a Feynman-Kac martingale.

steps.slogan: Cancel the paths that stop away from $x_0$ by flipping one sign.
steps.detail: If $X_T = x \ne x_0$ then $\Phi_x(T) = 0$, and flipping $\sigma_x$ changes only the sign of the martingale, so the sum over signs vanishes there.

steps.slogan: Apply optional stopping and shift the field by $\sqrt{2u}$.
steps.detail: The sum over signs at time $T$ equals its value at time $0$, which is the Gaussian density at $\Phi$ with $\Phi_{x_0} = \sqrt{2u}$, and the energy is invariant under adding constants.

concepts.c:markov-chain: The process is a continuous-time Markov chain on the vertices of the graph.
concepts.c:local-time: The local times are the occupation times of the vertices.
concepts.c:gaussian-free-field: The pinned Gaussian free field is the independent field added to the local times.
concepts.c:stopping-time: The proof stops the chain when one local time reaches a prescribed level.
concepts.c:martingale: The transported Gaussian density is a uniformly integrable martingale.

As a matrix, $G_\Lambda=(I-P_\Lambda)^{-1}$, where $P_\Lambda$ is the transition matrix restricted to $\Lambda$, so $G_\Lambda$ inverts the killed [discrete Laplacian](c:discrete-laplace-operator) $-\frac1{2d}\Delta$. For a transient walk one can take $\Lambda=\mathbb Z^d$, and then $G(x,y)=\sum_{n\ge0}P^n(x,y)$.

new_concepts.name: local time
new_concepts.reminder: The local time $L_t^x$ measures how much time a process spends near the level $x$ up to time $t$.
new_concepts.definition: For a one-dimensional [Brownian motion](c:brownian-motion) $B$, the local time is the jointly continuous process $(L_t^x)_{t\ge0,x\in\mathbb{R}}$ such that $\int_0^tf(B_s)\,ds=\int_{\mathbb{R}}f(x)L_t^x\,dx$ for all bounded Borel functions $f$ and all $t$, almost surely. So $x\mapsto L_t^x$ is the [Radon–Nikodym derivative](c:radon-nikodym-derivative) of the occupation measure $A\mapsto\int_0^t1_A(B_s)\,ds$ with respect to [Lebesgue measure](c:lebesgue-measure). For a continuous [semimartingale](c:semimartingale) $X$, the same formula with $d\langle X\rangle_s$ in place of $ds$ defines $L_t^x$, which is then right-continuous in $x$.

statement: For a transient [Markov chain](c:markov-chain) on a finite set with [Green function](c:green-function) $G$, the occupation field of the [loop soup](c:markov-loop-soup) with intensity $\frac12$ has the same law as $\frac12\varphi^2$, where $\varphi$ is the [Gaussian free field](c:gaussian-free-field) with covariance $G$.

hypotheses.text: $X$ is finite, the symmetric conductances make $X$ connected, and the killing measure $\kappa$ is not zero, so $G = (M_\lambda - C)^{-1}$ exists.

$\mathcal{L}_\alpha$ is a [Poisson random measure](c:poisson-random-measure) on loops with intensity $\alpha\mu$, and $\widehat{\mathcal{L}}_\alpha$ is the sum of the [local times](c:local-time) of its loops.
$\varphi$ is a centered Gaussian vector indexed by $X$ with covariance $G$.

conclusion: $\mathbb{E}\, e^{-\langle \widehat{\mathcal{L}}_\alpha, \chi\rangle} = \det(I + M_{\sqrt\chi} G M_{\sqrt\chi})^{-\alpha}$ for all $\chi \ge 0$, and $\widehat{\mathcal{L}}_{1/2}$ has the same law as $\frac12\varphi^2$.

proofs.name: Equal Laplace transforms via a determinant
proofs.slogan: Compute the Laplace transform of the loop soup occupation field and of the squared Gaussian field, and find the same determinant at intensity one half.
proofs.scope: Outline of the proof of Theorem 9 a) in Le Jan (2010). The analytic extension in step 2 and part b) of the theorem are taken from the source.

roles.why: Transience makes the Green function exist and the trace series of the transition matrix converge.
The Poisson structure turns the loop measure into the Laplace transform of the soup by the exponential formula.
The covariance $G$ makes the Gaussian Laplace transform equal to the same determinant.

steps.slogan: Compute the bridge expectation of $e^{-\langle \hat l, \chi\rangle}$ with the Feynman-Kac formula.
steps.detail: With $k = \chi/\lambda$, the Feynman-Kac formula gives $\lambda_x \mathbb{P}^{x,x}_t(e^{-\langle \hat l,\chi\rangle} - 1) = [e^{t(P-I-M_k)}]_{xx} - [e^{t(P-I)}]_{xx}$ for the bridge of duration $t$.

steps.slogan: Integrate over durations to get the loop measure of $e^{-\langle \hat l,\chi\rangle} - 1$ as a log [determinant](c:determinant).
steps.detail: Expanding the exponentials and using $\int_0^\infty t^{n-1}e^{-t}dt/n! = 1/n$ gives $\sum_n n^{-1}[\operatorname{Tr}(P-M_k)^n - \operatorname{Tr}P^n] = -\log\det(I + GM_\chi)$ for small $\chi$. The source extends this to all $\chi \ge 0$ by analyticity.

steps.slogan: Apply the exponential formula of the Poisson loop soup to get its [Laplace transform](c:laplace-transform).
steps.detail: For a Poisson ensemble with intensity $\alpha\mu$, $\mathbb{E}\exp(-\sum_{l}\langle \hat l,\chi\rangle) = \exp(-\alpha\mu(1 - e^{-\langle \hat l,\chi\rangle}))$, which equals $\det(I + M_{\sqrt\chi}GM_{\sqrt\chi})^{-\alpha}$. Each occupation time has a [gamma distribution](c:gamma-distribution) with shape $\alpha$ and scale $G^{x,x}$.

steps.slogan: Compute the Laplace transform of $\frac12\varphi^2$ by a Gaussian integral.
steps.detail: The density of $\varphi$ is proportional to $e^{-\frac12 z^\top (M_\lambda - C) z}$, so $\mathbb{E}\,e^{-\frac12\langle\varphi^2,\chi\rangle} = \det(M_\lambda - C)^{1/2}\det(M_\lambda - C + M_\chi)^{-1/2} = \det(I + GM_\chi)^{-1/2}$.

steps.slogan: Identify the two laws because Laplace transforms on the positive orthant determine a law.
steps.detail: At $\alpha = \frac12$ the two Laplace transforms agree for every $\chi \ge 0$. Exponentials $e^{-\langle z,\chi\rangle}$ are dense in the continuous functions on the compactified orthant by Stone-Weierstrass, so the laws of $\widehat{\mathcal{L}}_{1/2}$ and $\frac12\varphi^2$ are equal.

concepts.c:gaussian-free-field: The Gaussian free field is the field whose square matches the soup occupation field.

concepts.c:local-time: The occupation field of a loop is its local time at each site.
concepts.c:determinant: Both Laplace transforms are powers of the same determinant.

new_concepts.name: Gaussian free field
new_concepts.reminder: The Gaussian free field is the centered Gaussian field whose covariance is the Green function of the Laplacian.
new_concepts.definition: The discrete Gaussian free field on a finite set $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^d$ with zero boundary values is the centered Gaussian vector $(\varphi_x)_{x\in\Lambda}$ with covariance $\mathbb E[\varphi_x\varphi_y]=G_\Lambda(x,y)$, the [Green function](c:green-function) of simple random walk killed when it leaves $\Lambda$. Its density is proportional to $\exp\big(-\frac1{4d}\sum_{x\sim y}(\varphi_x-\varphi_y)^2\big)$, with $\varphi=0$ outside $\Lambda$. In the continuum, the Gaussian free field is the centered Gaussian random distribution whose covariance is the Green function of the Dirichlet Laplacian.

new_concepts.name: loop soup of a Markov chain
new_concepts.reminder: A Poisson ensemble of unrooted loops of a Markov chain, with intensity a multiple of the loop measure.
new_concepts.definition: For a transient [Markov chain](c:markov-chain) with loop measure $\mu = \sum_x \int_0^\infty t^{-1}\lambda_x \mathbb{P}^{x,x}_t\,dt$ and $\alpha > 0$, the loop soup $\mathcal{L}_\alpha$ is a [Poisson random measure](c:poisson-random-measure) on loops with intensity $\alpha\mu$.

new_concepts.name: point process
new_concepts.reminder: A point process is a random locally finite set of points, described by the random counts it puts in sets.
new_concepts.definition: Let $E$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space with a countable base, and let $M_p(E)$ be the set of [Radon measures](c:radon-measure) on $E$ with values in $\{0,1,2,\dots,\infty\}$, which are the locally finite sums of [Dirac measures](c:dirac-measure). A point process on $E$ is a [random variable](c:random-variable) $N$ with values in $M_p(E)$, where $M_p(E)$ has the sigma-algebra generated by the maps $\mu\mapsto\mu(B)$ for Borel sets $B$. Each count $N(B)$ is then a random variable, and it is finite when $B$ is relatively compact.

new_concepts.name: Poisson random measure
new_concepts.reminder: A Poisson random measure puts independent Poisson numbers of points in disjoint sets, with means given by a fixed measure.
new_concepts.definition: Let $\mu$ be a [sigma-finite measure](c:sigma-finite-measure) on a measurable space $(E,\mathcal{E})$. A Poisson random measure with mean measure $\mu$ is a random measure $N$ on $E$ with values in $\{0,1,2,\dots,\infty\}$ such that $N(B)$ has the [Poisson distribution](c:poisson-distribution) with mean $\mu(B)$ for each $B$ with $\mu(B)<\infty$, and $N(B_1),\dots,N(B_k)$ are [independent random variables](c:independent-random-variables) for disjoint $B_1,\dots,B_k$. Such an $N$ exists for every sigma-finite $\mu$, and $\mu$ determines its law.

statement: Given the values of the [discrete Gaussian free field](c:gaussian-free-field) in $V$ outside a subset $U$, the field in $U$ is the [harmonic](c:harmonic-function) extension of these values plus an independent free field in $U$.

hypotheses.text: $V \subset \mathbb{Z}^d$ is finite, and $h$ is the [discrete Gaussian free field](c:gaussian-free-field) in $V$: its values on $V$ have density proportional to $\exp(-\frac{1}{4d}\sum_{x \sim y}(h_x - h_y)^2)$, and $h = 0$ off $V$.
$U$ is a nonempty subset of $V$, and $W = V \setminus U$.

conclusion: With $\varphi$ equal to $h$ off $U$ and discrete harmonic on $U$, $\varphi_x = \mathbb{E}[h_x \mid h_W]$, and $h - \varphi$ is independent of $h_W$ with the law of the free field $h^U$ in $U$.

proofs.name: Orthogonal splitting of the Dirichlet energy
proofs.slogan: Split each configuration into its harmonic extension and a remainder supported in $U$, and see that the Gaussian density factorizes.
proofs.scope: The whole theorem for finite $V$ in every dimension, with existence and uniqueness of the harmonic extension. Infinite $V$ is excluded.

roles.why: The density is the exponential of a negative quadratic energy, so a splitting of the energy factorizes the law.
The set $U$ fixes where the remainder lives and where the extension is harmonic.

steps.slogan: Sum by parts to show that the Dirichlet energy is a positive definite [quadratic form](c:quadratic-form).
steps.detail: For finitely supported $f, g$, $\sum_{x \sim y}(f_x - f_y)(g_x - g_y) = -\sum_x g_x \Delta f(x)$ with the [discrete Laplacian](c:discrete-laplace-operator) $\Delta$. A finitely supported $f$ with zero energy is constant on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and so vanishes, so the energy is positive definite on each finite set.

steps.slogan: Solve the discrete Dirichlet problem on $U$ with boundary values $h$ on $W$.
steps.detail: The equation $\Delta\varphi = 0$ on $U$ with $\varphi = h$ off $U$ is a linear system in $\mathbb{R}^U$. Its matrix has positive definite quadratic form by the previous step, so the solution exists, is unique, and depends linearly on $h_W$.

steps.slogan: Show that the energy of $h$ is the sum of the energies of $\varphi$ and $h - \varphi$.
steps.detail: The cross term equals $-\sum_x g_x \Delta\varphi(x)$ with $g = h - \varphi$. It vanishes because $g$ is zero off $U$ and $\Delta\varphi$ is zero on $U$. So $\mathcal{E}(h) = \mathcal{E}(\varphi) + \mathcal{E}(g)$.

steps.slogan: Shift the values in $U$ by $\varphi$ and factorize the density of $(g, h_W)$.
steps.detail: For fixed $h_W$ the shift $h_U = g + \varphi_U(h_W)$ preserves Lebesgue measure. By Fubini's theorem the joint density of $(g, h_W)$ is a product of $e^{-\mathcal{E}(g)/4d}$ and a function of $h_W$. So $g$ is [independent](c:independent-random-variables) of $h_W$ and is the free field in $U$.

steps.slogan: Identify $\varphi$ as the [conditional expectation](c:conditional-expectation) of $h$ given the values on $W$.
steps.detail: Since $\varphi$ is a function of $h_W$ and $g$ is independent of $h_W$ with mean zero, $\mathbb{E}[h_x \mid h_W] = \varphi_x$. The conditional law of $h_U$ is therefore the law of $\varphi_U$ plus a free field in $U$, which is the [Markov random field](c:markov-random-field) property of $h$.

concepts.c:gaussian-free-field: The discrete Gaussian free field is the random field whose conditional law the theorem describes.
concepts.c:harmonic-function: The conditional mean is the discrete harmonic extension of the outside values.
concepts.c:quadratic-form: The Dirichlet energy is a positive definite quadratic form, which makes the field Gaussian.
concepts.c:discrete-laplace-operator: The discrete Laplacian defines harmonicity and appears in the summation by parts.
concepts.c:independent-random-variables: The remainder field is independent of the values outside U.
concepts.c:conditional-expectation: Part (1) identifies the harmonic extension as a conditional expectation.
concepts.c:markov-random-field: The result is the Markov property of the free field as a random field.

source.ref: M. Biskup, Extrema of the two-dimensional discrete Gaussian free field (arXiv:1712.09972v4, 2019), Lemma 3.1 (Gibbs-Markov property), pp. 33-35.

statement: Two centered [Gaussian measures](c:gaussian-measure) on a separable [Hilbert space](c:hilbert-space) are either [equivalent](c:equivalent-measure) or [mutually singular](c:singular-measure). They are equivalent exactly when their [Cameron–Martin spaces](c:cameron-martin-space) coincide and $BB^* - I$ is a [Hilbert–Schmidt operator](c:hilbert-schmidt-operator), where $B = C_1^{-1/2}C_2^{1/2}$.

hypotheses.text: $H$ is a separable real [Hilbert space](c:hilbert-space).
$\mu_1 = N(0, C_1)$ and $\mu_2 = N(0, C_2)$ are centered [Gaussian measures](c:gaussian-measure) on $H$ with strictly positive covariance operators.

conclusion: Either $\mu_1 \sim \mu_2$ or $\mu_1 \perp \mu_2$, and $\mu_1 \sim \mu_2$ if and only if $C_1^{1/2}H = C_2^{1/2}H$ and $\|BB^* - I\|_{HS} < \infty$ with $B = C_1^{-1/2}C_2^{1/2}$.

proofs.name: Diagonalization and Kakutani's product criterion
proofs.slogan: Diagonalize the two Gaussian laws in a common basis up to an equivalence operator, then Kakutani's product criterion decides between equivalence and singularity.
proofs.scope: Outline of the proof of the Theorem of Feldman (1958) in the centered case, with a final step that translates Feldman's condition into the Hilbert-space form of Theorem 7.35 of Dashti and Stuart. Kakutani's criterion and von Neumann's perturbation theorem are taken from the source.

roles.why: Separability makes the functionals $\langle h, \cdot\rangle$ generate the Borel σ-field, so Feldman's theorem applies to measures on $H$.
All functionals are Gaussian under both measures, which gives product densities, and strict positivity gives $C_i^{1/2}$ a dense range.

steps.slogan: Densities on growing σ-fields converge by the [martingale](c:martingale) convergence theorem.
steps.detail: If the σ-fields $\mathcal{S}_N$ increase to $\mathcal{S}$, then $d\nu_N/d\mu_N \to d\nu/d\mu$ almost everywhere, so a zero limit means singularity and a finite nonzero limit means equivalence.

steps.slogan: Kakutani's criterion decides when a [product](c:product-measure) of one-dimensional Gaussian densities converges.
steps.detail: For independent standard normal $z_i$, the product $\prod_{i \le N} a_i e^{\frac12(1-a_i^2)z_i^2}$ tends to $0$ if $\sum(1-a_i^2)^2 = \infty$ and to a finite nonzero limit if the sum is finite.

steps.slogan: Perturb by an equivalence operator so that the correspondence gets pure point spectrum.
steps.detail: On each dyadic spectral piece of $\sqrt{R^*R}$, a small Hilbert–Schmidt perturbation from von Neumann's theorem gives pure point spectrum, and the pieces combine into an equivalence operator $U$.

steps.slogan: Build a reference measure equivalent to $\mu$ in which the coordinates are independent.
steps.detail: With $\|U^{-1}y_i\| = 1/a_i$, the measure $\mu'$ with independent $y_i \sim N(0, a_i^{-2})$ has $d\mu'/d\mu = \prod a_i e^{\frac12(1-a_i^2)y_i^2}$, and $\sum(1-a_i^2)^2 < \infty$ gives $\mu' \sim \mu$.

steps.slogan: Product densities in eigen-coordinates force either singularity or equivalence.
steps.detail: The coordinates $Z_i$ are independent with variances $1$ under $\mu'$ and $\alpha_i^2$ under $\nu$, so $d\nu_N/d\mu'_N = \prod \alpha_i^{-1}e^{\frac12(1-\alpha_i^{-2})Z_i^2}$ tends to $0$, which contradicts non-singularity, or to a nonzero limit.

steps.slogan: Translate the equivalence operator condition into the Cameron–Martin and Hilbert–Schmidt conditions.
steps.detail: The functionals $\langle h, \cdot\rangle$ identify each $L^2(\mu_i)$ closure with $H$ through $C_i^{1/2}$, the correspondence becomes $W = B^*$, and $W^*W - I = BB^* - I$.
